description: Biomedical / virology / pandemic-origins domain glossary. Specialized senses the COVID-origins corpus turns on that general WordNet lacks. Neutral, factual glosses. Loads via collapse_library_bulk like WordNet; disambiguation prior keys on domain='biomed'.

senses.gloss: research that experimentally increases a pathogen's transmissibility, host range, or virulence
research or mutation that reduces or removes a biological function of a pathogen
a pathogen modified to be more transmissible or virulent such that it could cause a pandemic
the U.S. HHS framework for reviewing and funding research on enhanced potential pandemic pathogens
forms: potential pandemic pathogen care and oversight

senses.gloss: a polybasic amino-acid motif at the S1/S2 junction of a coronavirus spike protein, cleaved by the host enzyme furin, that can enhance cell entry and transmissibility
a host cell enzyme (protease) that cleaves certain proteins, including some viral spike proteins
the surface glycoprotein a coronavirus uses to bind a host-cell receptor and enter the cell
angiotensin-converting enzyme 2, the human cell-surface receptor that the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein binds
repeatedly growing a virus through successive host cells or animals so it adapts, which can alter transmissibility or virulence
an engineered virus combining genetic material from two or more distinct viruses
constructing or modifying a virus from a cloned DNA copy of its genome
exchange of genetic material between genomes, naturally or by engineering
an infectious disease transmitted from animals to humans; a zoonotic spillover event
the hypothesis that an outbreak originated from a laboratory accident or release rather than natural spillover
biosafety level 4, the highest laboratory containment level, used for the most dangerous pathogens
a virology research institute in Wuhan, China, central to lab-origin questions about SARS-CoV-2
the coronavirus that causes COVID-19
a bat coronavirus, the closest known relative of SARS-CoV-2 at the time of its identification
an influential 2020 scientific paper arguing SARS-CoV-2 most likely had a natural origin
a 2018 EcoHealth Alliance / Wuhan Institute of Virology grant proposal to DARPA involving coronavirus engineering, including a proposed furin cleavage site insertion
a U.S. nonprofit that channeled NIH funding for coronavirus research, including subawards to the Wuhan Institute of Virology
a laboratory virus engineered to carry another virus's surface proteins for safe study of cell entry
genetically modified mice expressing human genes (e.g. human ACE2) used to study human-relevant infection
an animal species in which a pathogen adapts before transmitting to humans
the degree to which a pathogen causes disease or harm in its host
the capacity of a pathogen to spread from one host to another
weakening of a pathogen so it causes little or no disease, as in some vaccine production
an organism (virus, bacterium, etc.) that causes disease
a family of enveloped RNA viruses, some of which infect humans and cause respiratory disease
the complete set of genetic material of an organism or virus
